column1: # spec-coverage-scope-baseline.tsv — the frozen R-03 proof (ADR-0138 §D5, issue #312, Task 6).
# WHAT THIS IS. One row per (SPEC, declared id) pair in the completed (spec, plan) corpus, each
# carrying the SCOPED verdict spec-coverage.sh produces today: COVERED or UNSCOPED. This is a
# per-item FROZEN baseline, not a floor — CLAUDE.md rule 10 / ADR-0124: a >= N assertion over a
# population with slack still passes when its own plant removes one member; an exact per-row
# comparison is what a plant actually bites.
# HOW IT IS PRODUCED, EXACTLY (do not hand-edit a row without re-running this). The population is
# derived by issue-number prefix: for each docs/specs/<N>-*.spec.md that declares at least one
# R-NN id (spec_declares_ids()), find docs/superpowers/plans/<date>-<N>-*.md, falling back to
# docs/superpowers/plans/<date>-<slug>.md when the plan filename carries no bare issue number (the
# corpus has both forms). NEVER paired through a manifest — most manifests' artifacts.spec still
# points at the mutable root SPEC.md slot, which silently reduces to N copies of whichever feature
# is in flight. The chain currently producing THIS file is itself excluded from the population: an
# in-flight chain is not a completed corpus member. For every resolved (spec, plan) pair, every
# declared id's verdict is read straight off `spec-coverage.sh --spec <spec> --plan <plan>
# --tests-root <repo-root>`'s own stdout — COVERED / UNSCOPED / UNCOVERED — never re-interpreted.
# Since ADR-0166 (issue #460), the regeneration procedure for a SINGLE pair is
# script IS the per-pair derivation, reading verdicts straight off spec-coverage.sh's own stdout and
# never re-interpreting them. spec-coverage.test.sh's RS7-RS10 block (RS_PAIRS / RS_LIVE) is the
# loop AROUND it that sweeps the whole corpus and compares every row against this file; this file's
# rows must equal that sweep's output byte-for-byte or RS7/RS8a/RS8b fail on the specific diverging
# WHEN TO REGENERATE. Since ADR-0166 (issue #460), a completing concept-to-code chain bumps its own
# rows into this file at Step 7.0b (SKILL.md's `fence-contract: c2c-step7-baseline-bump` fence), so
# RS8b's "a live verdict with no baseline counterpart" red is no longer the ordinary way a new pair
# joins this corpus — the enrolling chain's own commit already carries the rows. The manual
# procedure below now applies only to the two cases the chain does not cover: a pair no chain
# enrolled (a hand-placed SPEC with no concept-to-code chain behind it), and a genuine drift signal
# (a later feature adding or renaming a test file that shifts an ALREADY-frozen pair's scope — RS7
# reporting that red is the mechanism working, not a false alarm to silence by re-freezing blindly).
# For either case, the same script the chain uses gives an operator two commands, never a hand-edit:
# prints a pair's current rows without writing anything; `--bump --baseline <this file> --spec
# <spec> --plan <plan> --tests-root <repo-root>` appends the rows absent from this file and refuses
# (exit 1, nothing written) when a computed row disagrees with an existing frozen one — never
# rewrite a row for a SPEC whose chain was already complete and frozen here (CLAUDE.md rule 14: a
# historical record is corrected forward, not in place).
# MEASURED 2026-08-14 (re-derive, do not trust this comment per CLAUDE.md rule 13): 15 (spec, plan)
# pairs, 117 declared ids, 93 COVERED, 24 UNSCOPED (20 classed testable, 4 classed
# not-test-assertable). RS9a/RS9b assert only a >= 15 / >= 100 vacuity floor on the DERIVATION
# (rule 10) — this file's 117 exact rows, compared row-by-row in RS7/RS8, are where R-03 is actually
# 2026-08-18 — REGENERATED UNDER ADR-0154 (Task 5, spec-coverage-scope-back-reference). The scope
# filter became a conjunction — a discovered test file must ALSO name the feature back, not only
# be named by the plan — see spec-coverage.sh's own header and ADR-0154 §D1/§D5. STARTING STATE,
# re-derived the same day rather than trusted from the 2026-08-14 sentence above (CLAUDE.md rule
# 13): 16 (spec, plan) pairs, 130 declared ids, 106 COVERED, 24 UNSCOPED. The corpus had already
# grown by one completed pair since 2026-08-14, for reasons unrelated to this feature and not
# investigated further here — out of this task's scope.
# The RS7/RS8 derivation (spec-coverage.test.sh, section RS7-RS10, which IS the regeneration
# procedure — no row below was hand-edited) was re-run against this same 16-pair corpus with
# ADR-0154's conjunction filter already in place (commit 2102eeb) and diffed, row by row, against
# every row already committed here. RESULT: ZERO verdict changes and ZERO row-count changes — the
# regenerated (spec, id, verdict) set is byte-identical to what was already committed. PER-ROW
# ACCOUNTING: none required (0 of 130 rows differ; no COVERED -> UNSCOPED flip, no UNSCOPED ->
# COVERED flip). This confirms ADR-0154's M4 prediction on this feature's own corpus: the
# back-reference conjunction narrows the wider 52-plan/263-file scope population (94 files dropped,
# per the ADR) without moving a single frozen verdict in the narrower (spec, id) corpus this file
# 2026-08-19 — REGENERATED UNDER ADR-0157 (issue #487, the cross-feature id collision). The two
# questions that were still being asked of the UNFILTERED discovered population — UNSCOPED vs
# UNCOVERED, and what SCOPE-EMPTY falls back to — now read a bounded population: the files the plan
# names (half 1), plus the files that claim THIS feature ($OWN_RE), plus the files that claim no
# feature at all. Excluded, and this is the whole change: a file that claims ANOTHER feature by a
# `#<n>` token, whose R-NN belongs to that SPEC's numbering. STARTING STATE, re-derived on the day
# rather than trusted from the sentence above (CLAUDE.md rule 13): 16 pairs, 130 ids, 106 COVERED,
# RESULT: 12 of the 130 rows change verdict, all of them UNSCOPED -> UNCOVERED, all 12 within the
# class ADR-0157 exists to close. ZERO row-count change, ZERO COVERED row moved in either direction —
# so no id lost coverage and none gained it; what changed is which REMEDY the 12 are told to apply
# ("write the test", not "name the file in your plan"). PER-ROW ACCOUNTING, each row's own reason
# Spot-checked by hand on 404/R-04 before freezing: the harness that DOES claim issue #404
# (stop-gate-path-predicate.test.sh) contains no R-04 token at all, while seven other features'
# harnesses do — which is precisely the mislabel, seen from the inside.
# ALL 12 flip on POSITIVE evidence, not on absence: every one of the 12 has its only mention in a file
# that claims a DIFFERENT feature. The intermediate design that dropped a file for merely failing to
# claim this feature produced the same 12 rows AND broke two assertions written for ADR-0138 (RS1,
# RX6), whose fixture is an unclaimed file the plan does not name. Measured, both designs land here;
# only one of them keeps the unclaimed state's remedy honest.
# The three rows already classed not-test-assertable (222/R-10, 404/R-14, 410/R-17) KEEP that class
# and their original reason; the ADR-0157 note is appended to it rather than replacing it. Their
# verdict token moved for the reason above, not because the classification was wrong.
# derivation, not the rows. spec-coverage.test.sh's RS_PAIRS/RS_LIVE loops (Task 3) now call
# spec-coverage-baseline-rows.sh's --pair and --rows instead of re-deriving the same two answers a
# second time inline, and a completing concept-to-code chain now bumps its own rows into this file
# at Step 7.0b (Task 5) instead of leaving an unattributable RS8b red for the next unrelated author
# to inherit and diagnose from this header alone.
# RE-DERIVED STATE, same day, through the new call path (CLAUDE.md rule 13 — do not trust this
# comment, re-derive it): 16 (spec, plan) pairs, 130 declared ids, 130 baseline rows — 106 COVERED,
# 12 UNCOVERED, 12 UNSCOPED. RS7 (the frozen per-row comparison) reports ZERO divergence; RS8a and
# RS8b report ZERO orphans in either direction (verified by hand: the plant that mutates
# 176-worktree-isolation-contract.spec.md's R-01 row still turns RS7 red through the new call path).
# 0 OF 130 ROWS CHANGED — no verdict, class or reason column moved, and no row was added or removed.
# See ADR-0166 §M1 for the correction to SPEC.md's R-08 parenthetical ("16 live pairs, 16 baseline
# rows"), which understated the row count by an order of magnitude: 16 is the pair count, not the
# 2026-08-24 — CORPUS GROWTH (VCS-034, do_pair()'s issue-less SPEC resolution bug). do_pair()'s
# fallback slug stripped the first hyphen segment of a SPEC's basename UNCONDITIONALLY, even when
# that segment was not the numeric issue prefix. An issue-less SPEC built a mutilated fallback
# slug that never matched its real plan, so the pair silently never resolved and the SPEC never
# entered RS_PAIRS. Fixed in do_pair() (spec-coverage-baseline-rows.sh) to strip only when the
# first segment is actually numeric. Two previously-excluded issue-less SPECs now resolve and
# their rows are appended below via --bump (pure append, verified: `git diff -U0` shows 0 removed
# PER-PAIR ACCOUNTING (re-derived via --rows before bumping, CLAUDE.md rule 13):
# RE-DERIVED STATE, same day: 21 (spec, plan) pairs, 190 baseline rows (154 + 36). NO EXISTING ROW
# WAS TOUCHED — every new row is a pure append from --bump, never hand-written. The two new
# UNCOVERED rows below carry only the 3-column form --bump/--rows always writes (verdict, no
# class/reason) — RS7/RS8 read only the first 3 columns (spec, id, verdict), so this is
# functionally complete; the class/reason columns on older rows are hand-added documentation from
# earlier manual freezes, not a requirement of the format.
# NO ARCHIVED SPEC IS EDITED FOR THIS FILE (CLAUDE.md rule 14, ADR-0138 §D5). Retro-fitting
# `(no-test: ...)` into the 4 completed SPECs behind the not-test-assertable rows below would
# correct a historical record in place. This file is a new record ABOUT that corpus, written
# forward; `no-test:` (ADR-0138 §D4) governs SPECs written from now on, this baseline governs the
# 2026-08-24 — CORRECTION (VCS-035, PR #509, feat/commit-outcome-backstop-hook). PR #509 added a
# new test file, commit-outcome-backstop.test.sh, for an issue-less feature (no #<n> to claim with —
# the same gap VCS-034 names in do_pair()). Its R-01..R-10-ish assertion labels reuse this
# baseline's own R-NN vocabulary and are UNCLAIMED (no #<n> token), the same population ADR-0138
# always allowed a stranger's mention to sit in — rule 18's disclosed limitation, not a new defect.
# TWO ROWS FLIP CLEANLY, matching ADR-0157's own established direction (a stricter remedy, no
# coverage gained or lost): 222/R-07 and 404/R-04 move UNCOVERED -> UNSCOPED, because the new
# unclaimed file's mention re-joins the unscoped-question population alongside the pre-existing
# foreign-claimed one — exactly ADR-0138's original state for an unclaimed mention.
# ONE ROW DOES NOT FLIP, ON PURPOSE: 222/R-03 computes live as COVERED, but this is a false
# positive and is NOT accepted here. sync-manual-steps.test.sh is a pre-existing file already IN
# SCOPE for #222 (its plan names it, it names the plan back); PR #509 added an unrelated R-03
# mention to that SAME file for the commit-outcome-backstop feature. Scope-matching in
# spec-coverage.sh is FILE-granular, not per-mention, so the stray token is misread as covering
# #222's R-03. Freezing COVERED here would launder a wrong verdict into another feature's
# permanent record (CLAUDE.md rule 14) — left UNSCOPED instead, its true state, which means RS7
# is EXPECTED to keep reporting exactly this one row as diverging (live COVERED vs. frozen
# UNSCOPED) until the file-granularity gap itself is fixed (tracked under VCS-034/VCS-035, not
# fixed in PR #509 — the earlier attempt at the do_pair() half of this surfaced a much wider
# blast radius and was reverted, commit ba1cba6).
# PER-ROW ACCOUNTING (all three divergent rows, of 154 live pairs — RS7's own count):
#   222-vendor-deployed-only-skills  R-03 (left UNSCOPED, live diverges as COVERED — not corrected)
#   testable            — genuine drift: the gate was silently passing this id via a foreign or
#                          unlisted test-file mention before scoping landed.
#   not-test-assertable — a documentation, process, or external-process obligation with nothing
#                          executable to assert; the residual false-negative class ADR-0138 §D4
#                          exists to exempt going forward via (no-test: ...).
#   foreign-mention-only — the id's only in-population mention belongs to ANOTHER feature's SPEC,
#                          which numbers its requirements from R-01 like every other one. Added by
#                          ADR-0157; these rows carry UNCOVERED, not UNSCOPED, because there is no
#                          test of this feature to bring into scope.
# A line beginning with "#" in column 1 is a comment; spec-coverage.test.sh's RS8b skips it
# explicitly (`case "$_bn" in \#*) continue ;; esac`) and neither RS7 nor RS8a reads this file's
# lines directly (they iterate the LIVE side and probe the baseline only for a specific (bn, id)
# pair), so a comment line cannot be mistaken for a stray (bn, id) row on either check.
